wood-handbook-2021: Forest Products Laboratory (2021). Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material. General Technical Report FPL-GTR-282, USDA Forest Service. Chapter 5 (green density, modulus of elasticity and rupture; closest listed species used as proxy).
en-1991-1-4: EN 1991-1-4:2005 Eurocode 1, Actions on structures, Part 1-4: Wind actions. Air density 1.25 kg/m3, F = 0.5 rho cd A v^2, peak velocity pressure (1 + 7 Iv) q_m.
en-1991-1-3: EN 1991-1-3:2003 Eurocode 1, Actions on structures, Part 1-3: Snow loads. Used for the order of magnitude of snow and ice accretion (about 10 kg/m2 on plan area).
vogel-1989: Vogel, S. (1989). Drag and reconfiguration of broad leaves in high winds. Journal of Experimental Botany 40(8), 941-948.
mayhead-1973: Mayhead, G. J. (1973). Some drag coefficients for British forest trees derived from wind tunnel studies. Agricultural Meteorology 12, 123-130.
koerner-1979: Koerner, C., Scheel, J. A. and Bauer, H. (1979). Maximum leaf diffusive conductance in vascular plants. Photosynthetica 13(1), 45-82.
jones-2014: Jones, H. G. (2014). Plants and Microclimate, 3rd ed., Cambridge University Press. Leaf energy balance, leaf area index, boundary-layer conductance.
monteith-unsworth-2013: Monteith, J. L. and Unsworth, M. H. (2013). Principles of Environmental Physics, 4th ed., Academic Press. Penman-Monteith leaf transpiration.
pretzsch-2015: Pretzsch, H., Biber, P., Uhl, E. et al. (2015). Crown size and growing space requirement of common tree species in urban centres, parks, and forests. Urban Forestry and Urban Greening 14(3), 466-479.
